text:
Anya Patel: Quick Q — for the upcoming merit cycle: are salary increases applied retroactively to the start of the quarter, or do they take effect on the approval/payroll date? Also, if someone gets promoted and that changes PTO accrual, is that backdated?
Maya (People Ops): Short answer: most salary changes are effective the pay period after approval due to payroll cutoffs. We can backdate in limited cases up to the start of the quarter, but it needs a payroll exception. PTO accrual changes follow the effective date in Workday; we don't usually retro-adjust accruals.
Anya Patel: Thx — what's considered a "limited case" for backdating? manager forgot to submit on time, or retrospective performance decision?
Maya (People Ops): Limited cases = documented approval before the end of the quarter but entered after payroll closed. Example: VP approval email dated 03/28 but submitted 04/05 -> payroll exception can cover backpay to 03/28. If approval happened after quarter end, we can't backdate to that quarter. We need the approval artifact (email/workflow audit) + manager sign-off.
Samir Chen: Is there a cap on how far back payroll will go if exception approved?
Maya (People Ops): Yes — payroll will consider backpay up to one quarter retroactive (90 days) from the approval timestamp, and we run it through the payroll vendor for tax/regulatory checks. Anything older needs legal review.
Rafael Gomez: How does equity get handled on promotion? Does vesting schedule change or do we issue a refresh grant?
Maya (People Ops): Equity is separate from base salary. Common patterns: 1) title change alone — no automatic change to vesting; 2) promotion + compensation increase — manager/People Ops may propose a refresh or one‑time grant; 3) leveling bump to a different grant band — may trigger an equity adjustment. Each award requires appropriate approvals and will have its own grant date (not retro).
Jenna Liao: So equity grant date is never backdated to when the manager verbally offered? That's important for tax + strike price.
Maya (People Ops): Correct — grant date is system date when legal signs off. Verbal or offer emails don't change the grant date. We keep email thread as evidence but the grant must be issued in the system.
Anya Patel: For appeals — if an IC disagrees with leveling or comp outcome, what's the timeline and process?
people-ops-bot: Reminder: appeals window = 14 calendar days from manager notification. Submit appeals via: https://intranet.redwood.com/hr/appeals-form (requires manager and people-ops acknowledgement).
Maya (People Ops): Addendum: appeals should include specific evidence (examples, docs, peer feedback) and be routed by the employee to the manager first. If unresolved, escalate to people ops with the appeal form. People Ops will coordinate calibration committee review.
Samir Chen: Manager checklist for promotion submissions — can we get a short snippet we can paste into a PRD/OKR note?
Maya (People Ops): Yup. Quick paste-friendly checklist:
```
- Manager justification (role change + impact)
- Recent concrete examples (3–5 bullets)
- Updated org chart line item
- Proposed salary + equity recommendation
- Manager approval email (VP or director)
- HR/People Ops packet (Workday submission ID)
```
Rafael Gomez: Are raises prorated if they happen mid-pay-period?
Maya (People Ops): Raises are prorated on the pay period basis in payroll. If the effective date is mid-pay-period, payroll prorates the earnings for that period automatically.
Jenna Liao: Any tax implications we should flag to managers when they propose retro pay?
Maya (People Ops): Payroll will handle withholdings, but managers should note: retro pay can change tax withholding and may affect benefits deductions in some cases (401(k) limits, FSAs). People Ops will coordinate with Finance on large retro amounts.
Anya Patel: Is there a place with canned language for manager notifications when a promo/raise is approved? Helps keep comms consistent.
Maya (People Ops): Yes — we've got templates on the intranet. Quick example below managers can use for notification/email: 
```
Subject: Promotion & Comp Update
Hi <Name>,
Congratulations — effective <date>, your role will change to <New Title> and base salary will be updated to $<amount>. Your new equity grant (if applicable) will be processed separately with grant date and details to follow. Please reach out to me with any questions.
Thanks,
<Manager Name>
```
Samir Chen: One last: what about retroactive benefits coverage (e.g., changing health plan tier) — can that be backdated?
Maya (People Ops): Benefits enrollments are governed by carrier rules. We can request retroactive adjustments in narrow circumstances (eligibility change due to promotion effective date). Those require benefit carrier approval and sometimes employee signatures. People Ops will assist but can't guarantee carrier approval.
Rafael Gomez: Great — can People Ops drop the payroll cutoff dates for the upcoming cycle so managers know the latest submit-by date?
Maya (People Ops): Will do. We'll post the payroll cutoff + final submission date in #people-ops and update the intranet page by EOD tomorrow. If you need a one-off exception, DM me with the approval artifact. :white_check_mark:
Anya Patel: perfect, thanks everyone!
